text:
Jackson Blake was a fourth-round pick in 2021. He's now on an 11-game point streak for the defending champions, five goals and eight assists, which NHL.com's Tom Gulitti noted was second only to Connor McDavid's run this season.

The reason is opportunity, and he's earning it. Blake plays 17:51 a night, up from 16:30, and is on the ice for 83% of Carolina's power-play chances after 40% last season. He has 21 points in 21 games, 1.00 a game against 0.65 last year, and Carolina gets 66% of the 5v5 expected goals (the quality of chances) with him out there, the best mark on a team that drives play as well as anyone.

Two flags pull in opposite directions. The Hurricanes have scored 5.6 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, which will fade. But Blake himself has only six goals on 8.6 expected, and All Three Zones tracking put him in the 88th percentile for chances from the slot. The assists may slow down; the goals look like they've been waiting.
headline: Jackson Blake's 11-game streak has a foundation
